implementation_notes: The modern C++ default is gMock's ON_CALL together with WillByDefault(Return(...)): it defines what the mocked method answers without creating the expectation that the call must happen, which is exactly the stub contract - canned indirect inputs. Mock methods are declared with MOCK_METHOD in a class deriving from the collaborator's abstract interface, and NiceMock silences the 'uninteresting call' warning for methods the test does not care about. The gMock cookbook states the stub-versus-mock boundary in one line - 'use ON_CALL by default, and only use EXPECT_CALL when you actually intend to verify that the call is made' - so a stubbed test reads as behaviour without an interaction expectation. The generated mock replaces the hand-written stub subclass; a hand-written class implementing the abstract interface is still the right choice when GoogleTest must not enter the build or when the double needs real behaviour.
pitfalls: ON_CALL must be set before the mock is handed to the code under test; a default action registered after a matching call has already happened does not change that call.
Adding EXPECT_CALL to a method that only needed canned answers attaches an expectation the test never intended, so a refactoring that stops calling it turns green into red.
Non-virtual, static and final methods cannot be mocked by inheritance, and the mock object must outlive the SUT; keep both in the fixture and pass the interface by reference.

variants.name: Hand-written subclass of the abstract interface
variants.idiom_name: test class deriving from the pure-virtual interface with hard-coded returns
variants.implementation_notes: Without a framework the classic structure is written out: declare the collaborator as an abstract class (pure virtual functions and a virtual destructor), then derive a test class whose methods return the canned values, and pass it to the SUT by reference or pointer - the compiler checks each override and no reflection is involved. Prefer it when the double is small, when GoogleTest must not enter the build, or when the double should carry a little real behaviour (a counter, a stored argument) that a generated mock would not have. It is what ON_CALL/WillByDefault replaces, and the two compose: a hand-written fake used as the delegate of a mock (DelegateToFake) is the gMock recipe for a double that must behave.
pitfalls: A missing override specifier hides a signature drift: the method becomes a new non-virtual overload and the SUT keeps calling the base's pure virtual.
An interface with pure virtual functions needs a virtual destructor, or deleting through the base pointer is undefined behaviour when the stub is heap-allocated.
Passing the stub by value slices it to the abstract base; inject through a reference or pointer so the SUT sees the override.
